A warm welcome from Rachael, Headteacher, and Frank, Head of Security and Wellbeing
We’re proud to announce that Ofsted has rated Hove Micro-School Good overall, with Outstanding for both Behaviour & Attitudes and Personal Development.
Inspectors praised our “safe place to learn” where pupils are “understood and lovingly nurtured” — a calm, homely environment where anxious learners rediscover confidence, curiosity, and joy.​
At Hove Micro-School, every child is known, every strength is celebrated, and every need is met with care. Ofsted recognised our "special atmosphere", created by:
Skilled, compassionate staff who personalise learning for each child.
Strong focus on wellbeing and emotional growth.
Creative, tailored teaching that helps children achieve and thrive.
Rich, real-world experiences — from mindfulness walks to community projects.
We’re delighted that inspectors confirmed we meet all the independent school standards, and even more delighted that they saw what makes our approach special: love, patience, and purposeful learning.
Welcome to Hove Micro-School
Next Open Morning - Friday 27th November10:30-12:30
​Here at Hove Micro-School, we provide a nurturing, personalised learning environment across KS1, KS2, and KS3, where every child's unique needs are at the heart of our ethos. We offer small class sizes, experienced teachers, and a flexible, child-led curriculum that supports both academic progress and emotional wellbeing. We specialise in working with children with a range of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and school-based anxieties, ensuring that each child is equipped with the individualised tools that they need to thrive at school and beyond.
Watch our report on ITV News!
Science in the bedroom, geography in the living room - the south's first 'micro school' | ITV News Meridian
Hear from our Children and Parents
Check out what the children and parents think of Hove Micro-School
What is a Micro-School?
Read our blog exploring what micro-schools are and the key benefits for children and parents.
Read our latest article in The Argus!
Hove Micro School expands to allow more students and teachers | The Argus
Our Aims and Values
Our key ethos is to fit the school around the child instead of making the child fit into the school.
We believe that education should not be a 'one size fits all' concept. Mainstream school may not be the best fit for all children and we want to provide an alternative option for parents and children in our community.
The beauty of a micro-school is the care and attention provided is much greater and curriculum adaptations can be made to fit the needs and interests of your child. At Hove Micro-School, your child's interests and passions have a direct impact on the curriculum: it is truly a child-centred approach to learning.
Parents, teachers, and pupils influence the curriculum as a team to not only provide a tailor-made education for the children involved, but also to foster and grow a democratic community, founded on collaboration and mutual respect.
How our curriculum works...
'Before our daughter started attending HMS, she was experiencing school refusal and extreme anxiety. The nurturing, gentle and child-led approach used by the wonderful staff here, has allowed our daughter to once again feel safe, happy and able to enjoy learning again. She is like a completely different child and it's all thanks to micro school!'

Rachael Ammari BA (Hons), PGCE, MA
Founder and Headteacher
Welcome to Hove Micro-School!
As the founder and headteacher, I am proud to lead an educational environment that prioritises personalised learning and strong relationships. With a background in both private and state schools in the UK and the US, and holding a PGCE and Master’s in Education from the University of Sussex, my approach to education is informed by years of experience and research. My Master’s work was focused on attachment theory and the importance of relationships in education, which is central to the ethos of our school.
At Hove Micro-School, we believe that a child’s sense of security and connection is key to unlocking their full potential. Our small class sizes, with a maximum of eight pupils, ensure that each child receives individual attention in a nurturing environment. This allows us to develop a bespoke curriculum that adapts to the unique needs and interests of the children, while maintaining the essential social interaction of a peer group. We work closely with parents, ensuring that their input is valued and integrated into their child’s educational experience.
Hove Micro-School offers a premier, personalised education where every child is seen, supported, and encouraged to thrive. I am excited to share this journey with you and to provide a learning experience that truly focuses on the whole child.

Hove Micro-School is a unique educational setting based in a home environment. All classes are taught by experienced, fully qualified teachers, ensuring a high-quality education tailored to the needs of each child. With small class sizes of no more than eight children, we provide a nurturing and focused learning experience where individual attention is at the heart of everything we do.
A core element of our approach is that children help shape their own learning. Every half term, children select topics that interest them, and our team of teachers designs lessons around these themes, incorporating core subjects such as Maths, English, Science, and Humanities. This flexibility ensures that the curriculum is engaging, relevant, and inspiring, while still meeting key educational goals.
At Hove Micro-School, we place a strong emphasis on emotional wellbeing. Our small class sizes foster close relationships between children and teachers, creating a safe and supportive environment where children feel valued and confident. This focus on emotional health enables children to thrive both academically and personally.
Outdoor learning is a key part of our daily routine. We make full use of our allotment, located just behind the house, where children can engage in hands-on activities such as gardening, plant care, and nature observation. This regular interaction with the natural world reinforces practical learning and encourages a connection to the environment.
Our goal is to offer a dynamic, enriching education, with a strong focus on emotional wellbeing and the individual needs of every child.

SEND
At Hove Micro School, we offer a personalised learning experience within a nurturing and inclusive environment that caters to a wide range of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Our small class sizes, with a maximum of eight students, allow us to provide individualised attention, using PDA-appropriate language while maintaining clear boundaries and ensuring essential skills are covered.
Our teachers guide students in a low-demand manner, helping them to make choices and take ownership of their learning, all while ensuring that the curriculum is followed. Each term, students collaboratively select a topic that is integrated across lessons, encouraging engagement and curiosity. They also have the flexibility to opt out of activities and pursue personal projects, fostering both independence and a love for learning in a safe and supportive environment.
Inclusivity is at the heart of our approach, with students encouraged to take breaks whenever necessary and access sensory-friendly breakout spaces that support their emotional and sensory needs. Our team, which includes trained mental health first aiders, offers one-on-one emotional support, using tailored interventions to help children understand and regulate their emotions in a supportive and understanding way.
We embrace multi-sensory and project-based learning to ensure lessons are both engaging and accessible. Resources are personalised, including tools such as communication cards, energy check-ins using the ‘spoons’ metaphor, and visual guides designed to reflect each child's individual interests.
Our expertise in SEND is broad, supporting children with Autism, ADHD, trauma-informed responses, Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA), dyslexia, Emotional Based School Avoidance (EBSA), speech and language difficulties, sensory processing differences, dyspraxia, dyscalculia, anxiety disorders, attachment difficulties, and social communication challenges. However, due to the nature of our cohort and small size, we are unable to cater for severe behavioural issues. Our deep understanding of these needs ensures that every child receives the tailored support they deserve.
We are also committed to advancing SEND knowledge within our team. Our neurodiversity training, led by neuro-affirming providers, equips staff with the skills needed to effectively support our children.
With a high staff-to-student ratio, a strong focus on mental health, and a commitment to celebrating neurodiversity, Hove Micro School creates an environment where every child is valued, supported, and empowered to reach their full potential.
